territory: Feed, posts, comments, likes, polls, bookmarks, reports: src/app/(main)/feed/** (actions.ts read in full), src/lib/{posts,post-visibility,post-visibility-rule,rich-text-editing,city-scope,social,content-view}.ts, src/components/posts/** (all 12 files), the letters surfaces that render Post rows (letters index, letters/[id], letters/[id]/edit, drafts-strip, letter-engagement), plus the supporting libs they call (validators, member-gate, rate-limit, storage, upload-ownership-rule, collection-intake, account-purge, search-log, utils rich-text/date helpers) and prisma/schema.prisma models Post/Comment/Like/Bookmark/PollOption/PollVote/CommentLike/Report/Notification.

findings.title: Deleting or editing a post from the feed leaves the stale card on screen: the client posts state has no removal/update path
findings.expected: After the author deletes a post (or saves an edit in the quick-edit dialog), the card disappears (or shows the new text) immediately, the way admin moderation and fresh posting already do.
findings.actual: The card stays on screen with its old content until the member navigates away and back or reloads. Delete shows no success feedback at all; edit shows a success toast while the card keeps the old text.
findings.evidence: PostCard.handleDelete is `const result = await deletePost(post.id); if (result.error) toast.error(result.error);` — there is NO success branch: no setRemoved, no callback to the list. EditPostDialog.handleSubmit on success does only `toast.success(...); onClose();`. The feed list lives in CLIENT state: PostFeed holds `const [posts, setPosts] = useState<PostData[]>([])`, filled by `loadPosts` in an effect keyed on `[fetchPosts, reloadKey, groupId, scope, sortBy, search, timeFilter]` — deletePost's `revalidatePath("/feed")` re-renders server components but can never touch that useState, and nothing bumps reloadKey (FeedColumn only bumps it via the composer's onPosted). The asymmetry is visible in the same file: the ADMIN path does handle it (`if (!result.error) setRemoved(true)` in handleModerationConfirm, with the comment "Removed optimistically ... rather than waiting on the revalidatePath round trip"), and CommentsSection removes deleted comments locally via removeLocally(). Only the author's own delete and edit were left out. Same gap in ProfileAuthorFeed (same PostCard, same client state) and the saved-posts masonry.
findings.fixDirection: Give PostCard an onDeleted callback (mirroring onBookmarkChange) that the author-delete success path calls, plus setRemoved(true) locally; have PostFeed/ProfileAuthorFeed/SavedPostsFeed drop the id from their state. For edits, return the saved content from editPost (it already returns success) and either lift it into local card state (a `const [content, setContent] = useState(post.content)` mirror) or pass an onEdited callback that patches the posts array. Do the same for EditPostDialog used from the letters card.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: create a post as the test account, delete it from its card menu, `expect.poll` the card count to drop without navigation; edit a post and assert the card text updates in place.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account: post something on /feed, open the card's menu, Delete, confirm — observe the card remain until reload. Then edit a post's text via the dialog and observe the old text persist behind the success toast.

findings.title: votePoll double-click: unhandled P2002 on the vote unique constraint throws the action and leaves the poll permanently disabled
findings.expected: Two rapid taps on poll options record one vote; the second attempt is absorbed (P2002 treated as already-voted, like reportUser does), and the UI settles on the truth.
findings.actual: Both requests pass the check-then-insert (`const existing = await prisma.pollVote.findUnique(...); if (existing) {...} else { await prisma.pollVote.create(...) }`), the loser hits `@@unique([userId, postId])` and the action THROWS. Client-side, `handleVote` has `if (submitting) return` but `setSubmitting(true)` hasn't re-rendered between two same-frame taps, and it has no try/catch: `const result = await votePoll(postId, optionId)` rejects, so `setSubmitting(false)` on line 111 never runs — every option button carries `disabled={submitting}`, so the poll is dead until the page is remounted, with the optimistic vote still painted.
findings.evidence: actions.ts 284-307 is a bare find-then-create with no catch; the file's ONLY P2002 handler is in reportUser (report-action.ts:189 `err.code === "P2002"`), which proves the pattern was known and applied elsewhere. poll-display.tsx: `async function handleVote(optionId){ if (submitting) return; setSubmitting(true); ... const result = await votePoll(postId, optionId); if (result.error) {...revert...} setSubmitting(false); }` — no try/finally, so a rejected action skips both the revert and the re-enable.
findings.fixDirection: Server: wrap the create in try/catch, treat P2002 as success (or better: use `prisma.pollVote.upsert({ where: { userId_postId }, create: {...}, update: { pollOptionId } })`, which also removes the read-modify-write). Client: wrap the await in try/finally so setSubmitting(false) always runs, and revert optimistic state in catch.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test on the action calling votePoll twice concurrently for one user (or an integration test asserting upsert semantics); a security-regressions-style test asserting the action returns {success} not a throw on duplicate.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account on a test poll: double-tap two options as fast as possible; watch the network tab for a 500/digest error and the poll buttons stay disabled. Safe (only writes one PollVote row for the test account).

findings.title: toggleLike / toggleCommentLike / toggleBookmark check-then-write races throw unhandled P2002/P2025; no client handler catches the rejection
findings.expected: Double-tapping a heart (the single most common gesture in the app) ends in a consistent state: one like or none, matching what the UI shows.
findings.actual: Two concurrent calls both run `findUnique` then branch. Like path: both see null → both `create` → the loser throws P2002 (`@@unique([userId, postId])`, schema.prisma:465). Unlike path: both see the row → both `delete({ where: { id: existing.id } })` → the loser throws P2025 (record not found). The thrown action rejects the client await; handleLike in PostCard (`const result = await toggleLike(post.id); if (result.error) {...revert...}`), CommentItem.handleLike and handleBookmark all lack try/catch, so the revert never runs: an unhandled rejection is logged and the heart/count is left disagreeing with the DB until reload. LoveButton fires onToggle unconditionally on every click with no in-flight guard, so nothing upstream prevents the concurrency.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:486-494: `if (existing) { await prisma.like.delete({ where: { id: existing.id } }); } else { await prisma.like.create({ data: { userId, postId } }); ... }` — no catch anywhere in the four toggle actions. love-button.tsx handleClick: `function handleClick() { if (!liked) { setAnimate(true); ... } onToggle(); }` — no disabled/in-flight state.
findings.fixDirection: Server: make the toggles idempotent — catch P2002 as 'already liked' and use `deleteMany({ where: { userId_postId } })`-style deletes (deleteMany never throws on zero rows), or upsert/delete-by-compound-unique. Client: add try/catch around every toggle await with the existing revert logic, and/or an in-flight ref in the handlers.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test firing toggleLike twice concurrently for one (user, post) and asserting both resolve without throwing and exactly one Like row remains.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account: double-tap a heart rapidly on a test post; observe a rejected server-action response in the network tab and the heart state diverging from a reloaded page. Writes only the test account's own Like row.

findings.title: Replying to a reply notifies the ROOT comment's author, not the person the UI says you are replying to
findings.expected: The composer says "Replying to B" — B should receive the reply notification.
findings.actual: B never hears about it unless B also wrote the root comment. The 1-level-depth redirect rewrites parentId to the root BEFORE the notification target is chosen, and the client itself sends the root's id while displaying the reply author's name.
findings.evidence: Server (actions.ts 591-593): `if (parent.parentId) { parentId = parent.parentId; // reply to the root comment instead }` — then 639-657 notifies `parentComment.authorId` where parentComment is fetched by the REWRITTEN parentId, i.e. the root's author. Client (comments-section.tsx 343-352) makes it structural even without the redirect: replies' onReply sets `id: comment.deleted ? reply.id : comment.id` (the ROOT's id) while `name: reply.author!.name` — so the pill and placeholder read "Reply to <reply author>" (line 421) while the payload targets the root. The person named on screen is never the notification recipient for any reply-to-reply.
findings.fixDirection: Carry the ORIGINAL target through: keep the depth redirect for threading, but remember the pre-redirect parent's authorId (or accept a separate replyToUserId field validated to be a comment on the same post) and notify that person; keep notifying the root author only if they are a distinct third party, as today. Client: send the actual reply's id and let the server do the root redirect (it already does).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit/integration test: A posts, B comments, C replies to B, D replies to C's reply — assert D's action produces a notification for C (and post author A), not for B only.
findings.reproPlan: Live with two test accounts: reply to a reply, then check the named person's bell — no notification arrives; the root author gets "replied to your comment" instead.

findings.title: editPost caps plain posts at 5000 chars while createPost accepts 20000, so a legitimately created long post can never be edited
findings.expected: Per the letters spec ("content max becomes conditional: 5000 for 'post', 20000 for 'letter'"), the create and edit paths enforce the same per-kind cap; anything you could post you can edit.
findings.actual: postSchema is a flat `content: z.string().min(1).max(20000)` for BOTH kinds, and the composer has no length limit on the contentEditable (only a soft "This might make a lovely Letter" nudge at 600 chars). So a member can post 5001-20000 chars as a plain post through the normal UI. editPost then enforces `const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) return { error: ... }` — opening the edit dialog on such a post and saving (even with zero changes) is refused with "Content must be between 1 and 5000 characters".
findings.evidence: validators.ts:154 `content: z.string().min(1, "Post cannot be empty").max(20000)` with no kind conditionality; actions.ts:395-399 `const isLetter = post.kind === "letter"; const cap = isLetter ? 20000 : 5000; if (!content || content.length > cap) { return { error: \`Content must be between 1 and ${cap} characters\` }; }`. create-post-form.tsx has no maxLength on the editor (LETTER_NUDGE_LEN = 600 is explicitly "no red numbers, no limits messaging: just a hint").
findings.fixDirection: Make the caps agree: either refine postSchema to a conditional max (5000 when kind !== 'letter') so creation matches the spec, or raise editPost's post cap to 20000 to match what creation already allows. Pick one number and enforce it in both places from one shared constant.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test: create a 6000-char kind:'post' payload through postSchema and through editPost's validation, asserting the two verdicts agree.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account: paste ~6000 chars into the composer, post it (succeeds), then Edit and Save unchanged — refused with the 5000 error. Delete the test post after.

findings.title: createComment never verifies parentId belongs to postId: a crafted reply renders inside another post's thread and inflates the wrong post's count
findings.expected: Server actions are public HTTP endpoints: parentId must be validated as a comment ON the same post the comment is being written to (6c: Zod-validate everything including IDs and their relationships).
findings.actual: The parent check selects only `{ parentId: true, deletedAt: true, isHidden: true }` — never postId — so a caller who can view post A can pass a parentId from post B. The row is created with postId=A, parentId=(root on B). Consequences: (1) loadComments' rows query has NO postId constraint — `OR: [{ id: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }, { parentId: { in: rootIds }, ...VISIBLE_COMMENT }]` — so the comment RENDERS as a reply inside post B's thread while (2) it counts toward post A's `_count.comments` (which filters by postId), permanently desyncing A's count from A's visible thread; (3) the reply notification goes to B's root author even when B sits inside a private group the caller was never checked against (canViewPost ran on A only).
findings.evidence: actions.ts 581-594: `const parent = await prisma.comment.findUnique({ where: { id: parentId }, select: { parentId: true, deletedAt: true, isHidden: true } });` — no postId in the select and no `parent.postId !== parsed.data.postId` comparison anywhere. actions.ts 1147-1152 quoted above shows the thread fetch keyed purely on rootIds.
findings.fixDirection: Select postId in the parent lookup and refuse when `parent.postId !== parsed.data.postId` (same "That comment is gone" answer to avoid an oracle). Optionally also add `postId` to the loadComments rows where-clause as defense in depth.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the action: comment on post A with a parentId from post B must be refused. A -rule-style test is not possible (needs DB), so an integration test or a code-review regression grep.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would write a malformed row into the shared production database).

findings.title: Feed time filters (today/week/month/year) compute boundaries in server UTC, shifting every window 5h30m for IST members
findings.expected: "Today" for a member in India means since midnight IST; "This week/month/year" likewise anchor to IST boundaries.
findings.actual: getTimeFilterDate runs inside the server action on Vercel (UTC): `new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate())` is UTC midnight = 05:30 IST. A post written at 01:00 IST today is excluded from "Today" until it silently reappears the member's tomorrow; "This week" starts Sunday 05:30 IST (`d.setDate(d.getDate() - d.getDay())` on the UTC date); on the 1st of a month before 05:30 IST, "This month" still shows last month's window. This is the deeper query-window instance of the IST class — distinct from the already-tracked display-side toLocaleDateString note in bugs.md item 6.
findings.evidence: actions.ts 742-760: `case "today": return new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate());` etc., with `const now = new Date()` in a server action; the filter is applied as `createdAt: { gte: timeDate }` at line 831. Members are IST (brief), servers UTC.
findings.fixDirection: Compute the boundary in Asia/Kolkata: derive the IST calendar date (e.g. via Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone 'Asia/Kolkata' or by adding 330 minutes before truncating, then subtracting them back) and use that instant for gte. One helper, unit-testable with fixed clock values either side of 18:30 UTC.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on the extracted boundary helper: at 2026-08-21T20:00:00Z (01:30 IST Aug 22), 'today' must start at 2026-08-21T18:30:00Z, not 2026-08-21T00:00:00Z.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof needs a post written 00:00-05:30 IST and the filter checked before 05:30 IST).

findings.title: Keyset 'Load more' silently truncates the feed when the cursor post has been deleted
findings.expected: Pagination survives a row deleted at the page boundary: the next page picks up from the cursor's position or degrades gracefully.
findings.actual: The cursor is the last post's id (`cursor: { id: keysetCursor }, skip: 1`). deletePost is a HARD delete, so if that exact post is deleted between pages (author or admin), Prisma cannot locate the cursor row and `findMany` returns an empty list; the code then computes `hasMore = rows.length > PAGE_SIZE` = false and `nextCursor = null` — the member's "Load more" quietly ends the feed even though older posts exist, until a full refresh. The same failure exists for comment threads (loadComments cursors on a root comment id) in the narrower case of a root hard-deleted by account purge (soft deletes keep the row, so the ordinary delete path is safe there).
findings.evidence: actions.ts 874-885: `const keysetCursor = opts?.cursor && !opts.cursor.startsWith("offset:") ? opts.cursor : undefined; rows = await prisma.post.findMany({ where, include, orderBy: [{ createdAt: "desc" }, { id: "desc" }], take: PAGE_SIZE + 1, ...(keysetCursor ? { cursor: { id: keysetCursor }, skip: 1 } : {}) });` — Prisma's documented behavior for a non-existent cursor row is an empty result set, and nothing here distinguishes that from a genuine end of feed. Secondary: the offset branch (line 888) does `parseInt(opts.cursor.slice(7), 10) || 0` with no lower bound, so a crafted "offset:-1" makes Prisma throw on negative skip (self-inflicted only).
findings.fixDirection: Switch the cursor to VALUES rather than a row reference: pass the last row's (createdAt, id) and use a where-clause seek (`OR [ createdAt < c, { createdAt: c, id < lastId } ]`), which is immune to the cursor row disappearing. Alternatively detect the empty-page-with-cursor case and retry without the cursor from the last known createdAt. Clamp the offset branch to >= 0 while there.
findings.gateOrTest: Integration test: load page 1, delete the 20th post, request page 2 with the stale cursor, assert older posts still return.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account, feed with 21+ posts: scroll to get a cursor, delete the boundary post from another tab, press Load more — the feed ends early. Requires deleting only a test post.

findings.title: Post reports have no per-(reporter, post) dedupe: one member can file report after report on the same post, each paging the admins and opening a new thread
findings.expected: Same as user-flags: a second report of the same post by the same member is answered "we've already got it" without a second AdminThread or a second admin notification (reportUser does exactly this).
findings.actual: reportPost goes straight from the existence check to `prisma.report.create` — no findFirst against (reporterId, postId), and the schema constraint cannot help: `@@unique([reporterId, reportedUserId])` with the schema's own comment "Post reports carry reportedUserId = NULL, and Postgres treats NULLs as distinct in a unique index, so this constrains only user-to-user reports and leaves post reporting unaffected." Every duplicate creates a Report row, an AdminThread, a reporter notification, and notifyAdmins — bounded only by rateLimit('reports') at 10/24h plus the thread budget, so one motivated member can generate ~10 duplicate admin pages a day per post, indefinitely.
findings.evidence: report-action.ts 90-117: `const post = await prisma.post.findUnique(...); if (!post) return ...; const report = await prisma.report.create({ data: { targetType: "post", postId, reporterId: session.user.id, reason: trimmed } ... }); const thread = await openReportThread(...); await notifyAdmins(...)` — contrast reportUser's lines 166-172 (`const already = await prisma.report.findFirst({ where: { reporterId, reportedUserId, targetType: "user" } }); if (already) return { success: true, alreadyFlagged: true };`) plus its P2002 fallback.
findings.fixDirection: Mirror reportUser: findFirst on { reporterId, postId, targetType: 'post' } and return { success, alreadyFlagged } without a new thread; back it with a partial unique index in a manual migration (`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON "Report" ("reporterId", "postId") WHERE "targetType" = 'post'`) and catch P2002 the same way, since Prisma's schema can't express the partial index (same pattern as the lower() indexes note).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit/integration: reportPost twice for the same (reporter, post) → second returns alreadyFlagged and creates no second AdminThread row.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would page the real admin account twice).

findings.title: deletePost/deleteDraft delete R2 images BEFORE the row delete, inverting the ordering rule account-purge documents; a failed row delete strands a live post with dead images
findings.expected: Bytes are deleted only after the row delete succeeds — account-purge.ts states the invariant: "bytes are deleted only AFTER the row delete succeeds, because if the delete throws and rolls back, the member still exists and their images must keep rendering."
findings.actual: deletePost runs `await deletePostImages(post.images); await prisma.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } });` and deleteDraft the same. If `post.delete` then fails (pooler timeout, transient DB error — exactly the 6k chaos case), the post survives with every image URL returning 404/broken forever; delImage is irreversible. deleteDraft has the identical ordering for draft letters. (The reverse leak — row gone, delImage silently failing — is bounded and acknowledged, but this direction is user-visible corruption.) Related orphan in the same file: editPost's draft image rewrite (lines 409-445) replaces the `images` array without deleting the R2 objects for URLs dropped from the draft, and no cron/sweep exists anywhere under src/app/api to collect unreferenced upload objects.
findings.evidence: actions.ts 336-339: `// Delete image files\n  await deletePostImages(post.images);\n  await prisma.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } });` — and 250-252 in deleteDraft. account-purge.ts 79-86 quotes the correct ordering with its rationale, written by the same codebase for the same operation.
findings.fixDirection: Swap the order in deletePost and deleteDraft: delete the row first, then best-effort delImage of the collected URLs (delImage already never throws). For editPost's draft image swap, diff old vs new arrays and delImage the removed ones after a successful update.
findings.gateOrTest: Code-level regression test or review gate asserting `post.delete` precedes deletePostImages in both actions (grep-based check in the write-path reviewer's checklist).
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (proving it live requires inducing a DB failure mid-action).

findings.title: Missing indexes on hot foreign keys: Like.postId, Bookmark.postId, PollVote.postId/pollOptionId, CommentLike.commentId, Comment.parentId, Post.authorId
findings.expected: Every column the feed aggregates or cascades on has an index; at 2,000 users the Like table (plausibly 10^5-10^6 rows) must never be sequentially scanned per feed page.
findings.actual: Like, Bookmark, PollVote and CommentLike each carry only `@@unique([userId, ...])` — userId-leading, unusable for lookups by postId/commentId/pollOptionId. Every loadPosts/loadSavedPosts page computes `_count: { select: { comments: {...}, likes: true } }` plus per-option `_count: { select: { votes: true } }`, which Prisma resolves as aggregates keyed by postId/pollOptionId — full scans of those tables per page without the index. Postgres also checks FK references on every DELETE: a hard post delete scans Like/Bookmark/PollVote by postId, and a user purge cascade scans Comment by parentId (unindexed) once per deleted comment. Post has `@@index([groupId, createdAt])`, `([kind, createdAt])`, `([createdAt])` but nothing on authorId, so the profile Posts tab and collectImageUrls filter by authorId unindexed. Only Comment(postId, ...) was ever indexed (manual migration 2026-07-18).
findings.evidence: schema.prisma Like: `@@unique([userId, postId])` and nothing else (lines 457-466); Bookmark: `@@unique([userId, postId])` (428); PollVote: `@@unique([userId, postId])` only (616); CommentLike: `@@unique([userId, commentId])` only (627); Comment relations (447-450) with `@@index([postId, createdAt]) @@index([postId, isHidden])` but no parentId index; Post indexes at 414-416 lack authorId. grep of prisma/migrations-manual/ shows only Comment_postId_isHidden_idx was ever added by hand.
findings.fixDirection: Add `@@index([postId])` to Like and Bookmark, `@@index([postId])` and `@@index([pollOptionId])` to PollVote, `@@index([commentId])` to CommentLike, `@@index([parentId])` to Comment, `@@index([authorId, createdAt])` to Post — via a dated idempotent file in prisma/migrations-manual/ (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, never db push) plus the schema.prisma lines and prisma generate, per the repo's schema-change rule.
findings.gateOrTest: EXPLAIN ANALYZE the feed page's like-count aggregate before/after in Supabase (read-only), or the check-suite gaining a schema lint that every relation scalar has a covering index.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: run EXPLAIN on `SELECT "postId", count(*) FROM "Like" WHERE "postId" = ANY($1) GROUP BY 1` against the live DB and observe Seq Scan.

findings.title: No error handling on any feed client data path: a failed load leaves an infinite skeleton, a failed action leaves controls stuck disabled
findings.expected: 6k: DB slow/down mid-request — the member sees something actionable (an error line, a retry), and controls recover.
findings.actual: Every fetch is `promise.then(...)` with no .catch and every handler awaits without try/catch: (1) PostFeed's first-page effect — on rejection `setLoading(false)` never runs, the skeleton spins forever with no message; (2) handleLoadMore — `setLoadingMore(false)` skipped, the button reads "Loading..." permanently; (3) CommentsSection's initial loadComments — same infinite skeleton; (4) the IntersectionObserver page fetch — `loadingMoreRef.current = false` never resets, killing infinite scroll for the rest of the session; (5) comment handleSubmit — `setSubmitting(false)` skipped so the send button stays disabled with the member's text captive in the box; (6) same shape in ProfileAuthorFeed and SavedPostsFeed. On flaky mobile networks (the community's dominant access) these are routine, not exotic.
findings.evidence: post-feed.tsx 118-138: `fetchPosts(null).then((data) => { ... setLoading(false); ... });` — no catch. comments-section.tsx 166-173 inside the observer: `loadingMoreRef.current = true; const data = await loadComments(...); ... loadingMoreRef.current = false;` — an async IO callback with no try/finally. handleSubmit 191-205: `const result = await createComment(formData); ... setSubmitting(false);` — a rejection skips the last line.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap each await in try/catch/finally: finally resets the pending flag; catch shows a toast ("Couldn't load the feed — check your connection") and, for list loads, renders a retry affordance instead of the skeleton. A tiny shared helper (e.g. safeAction wrapper returning { error } on throw) would cover all seven sites uniformly.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright with route interception: abort the loadPosts action response and assert an error/retry state renders instead of a perpetual skeleton.
findings.reproPlan: Live via chrome-devtools MCP: open /feed, use network emulation to fail the next server-action request, trigger Load more — observe the button stuck at "Loading...".

findings.title: List queries lack the author self-exemption the single-post rule has: your own city-scoped post vanishes from your own feed, profile and letters index if you remove that city
findings.expected: decidePostVisibility establishes the rule: "Your own post is always yours" (authorId check before every scope check). The list queries should agree: an author always sees their own posts in their feed, their profile Posts tab, and the letters index.
findings.actual: loadPosts (non-admin) appends `cityScopeWhere(viewerCities)` unconditionally to AND, and cityScopeWhere is only `OR: [{ cityScope: null }, { cityScope: { in: viewerCities } }]` — no `{ authorId: viewer.id }` arm. A member who posts "Bengaluru only" and later removes Bengaluru from their UserPlaces loses sight of their OWN post everywhere it is listed (main feed, ProfileAuthorFeed via the same loadPosts, /letters index which spreads the same fragment), while canViewPost would still admit them — so a notification deep-link works but the lists deny the post exists, and they can no longer reach its card to edit or delete it. The batch-targeting OR (lines 838-843) has the same gap for legacy targetBatches rows.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:820 `if (!isAdmin) andConditions.push(cityScopeWhere(viewerCities));` composed into baseWhere with no author arm; city-scope.ts 20-27 shows the fragment; post-visibility-rule.ts:74 `if (post.authorId === viewer.id) return { ok: true, post };` is the single-post exemption the lists never mirror.
findings.fixDirection: Add `{ authorId: viewerId }` as an extra OR arm inside cityScopeWhere (take the viewer id as a parameter), and add the same arm to the batch-targeting OR in loadPosts and the letters index, so the list rule equals decidePostVisibility.
findings.gateOrTest: Extend post-visibility-rule.test.mjs's philosophy with an integration test: author with zero matching cities still receives their own city-scoped post from loadPosts.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account: add a city, post scoped to it, remove the city in settings, reload /feed and the profile Posts tab — the post is gone from both while its direct letter/notification URL still opens.

findings.title: Letter reading page and its generateMetadata skip the targetBatches check the visibility rule enforces — batch-targeted letters readable by direct URL
findings.expected: decidePostVisibility refuses "other-batch": a post/letter with targetBatches is visible only to viewers whose `${batchType}-${batchYear}` key appears in it. The letter page should give the same 404 it gives for other-city and drafts.
findings.actual: LetterPage hand-rolls the checks — isHidden, draft+author, group membership, canViewCityScope — but never consults targetBatches, so any signed-in member with the URL reads a batch-targeted letter in full (and generateMetadata leaks its real title the same way). This is precisely the divergence post-visibility.ts warns about ("security logic pasted into several files and then quietly diverging"); the page predates/bypasses the shared canViewPost. Mitigating: the current composer never sets targetBatches (no formData.set for it in create-post-form.tsx), so only legacy rows are affected today — but loadPosts, the letters index, and decidePostVisibility all still enforce it, so the field is live in every OTHER path.
findings.evidence: letters/[id]/page.tsx 93-106: the full check sequence is `if (isDraft && !isAuthor) notFound(); if (letter.groupId) {...membership...}; if (!(await canViewCityScope(letter.cityScope, session.user))) notFound();` — targetBatches never read. post-visibility-rule.ts 100-105: `if (post.targetBatches) { const key = \`${viewer.batchType}-${viewer.batchYear}\`; if (!post.targetBatches.includes(key)) { return { ok: false, reason: "other-batch" }; } }`.
findings.fixDirection: Replace the page's hand-rolled sequence (and generateMetadata's) with one call to canViewPost(letter-as-GuardedPost) / decidePostVisibility — the row is already fetched with every needed column — keeping the author-draft special handling it already gets from the rule.
findings.gateOrTest: Add a case to post-visibility-rule.test.mjs-style coverage asserting the letter page path uses the shared rule (integration test: other-batch viewer + targeted letter URL → 404).
findings.reproPlan: Live only if a legacy targetBatches letter exists (read-only check: query Post where targetBatches is not null); otherwise code-argument-only.

findings.title: Unverified members cannot save letter drafts, contradicting the codebase's own documented intent that drafts stay ungated
findings.expected: Per publishDraft's own comment: "Drafts themselves stay ungated on purpose: writing privately harms nobody, and somebody waiting on a confirmation email should not lose what they were working on." The gate should bite at publish, not at save.
findings.actual: The FIRST save of a fresh draft goes through createPost, which runs `requireVerifiedMember()` before ever reading saveAsDraft — and the gate requires both emailConfirmed AND verifyState === 'verified' (Stage 2). Resumed-draft autosave and manual saves go through editPost, which gates identically ("Editing is publishing again"). So a Stage 0/1 member who writes a long letter at /letters/new and clicks "Save as draft" is refused; their work exists only in the browser tab, which is exactly the loss the comment says the design avoids. Only deleteDraft and publishDraft's own flow treat drafts as private.
findings.evidence: actions.ts 48-57 (createPost): `const gate = await requireVerifiedMember(); if (!gate.ok) return { error: gate.error };` runs unconditionally; the saveAsDraft branch is only consulted at line 133. actions.ts 207-210 (publishDraft) carries the quoted intent comment. member-gate.ts 59-60: `if (!session.user.emailConfirmed) return {...EMAIL_UNVERIFIED}; if (session.user.verifyState !== "verified") return {...MEMBER_UNVERIFIED};`.
findings.fixDirection: In createPost, evaluate isDraft (kind letter + saveAsDraft) BEFORE the member gate and skip the gate for drafts (keep the rate limit); in editPost, skip the gate when the target row is the caller's own draft (the author+status check already runs). publishDraft keeps the gate, which is what actually protects the community.
findings.gateOrTest: Integration test: a user with verifyState 'pending' can createPost(saveAsDraft) and editPost their draft, but publishDraft is refused with MEMBER_UNVERIFIED.
findings.reproPlan: Live with an unverified test account: write at /letters/new, Save as draft — observe the verification dialog/toast instead of a saved draft.

findings.title: Like toggling is un-rate-limited and mints a fresh notification on every re-like: unbounded bell spam for the author
findings.expected: Toggling a heart on and off does not multiply notifications; write actions are metered (the file's own M2 pattern: posts and comments both call rateLimit).
findings.actual: toggleLike and toggleCommentLike have NO rateLimit call (grep confirms the file's only two are 'posts' at line 60 and 'comments' at line 561), and each like-after-unlike creates a brand-new Notification row (`prisma.notification.create` inside the create branch, with no dedupe against an existing like-notification for the same (actor, post) and no cleanup on unlike). A member holding the heart in a toggle loop generates one DB write pair + one notification per cycle, limited only by network round-trip: the author's bell fills with dozens of identical "X liked your post" rows. The 100-per-user prune bounds the table, not the experience, and votePoll/toggleBookmark share the missing meter (bookmark at least writes no notification).
findings.evidence: actions.ts 465-475: gate then straight to the toggle — no `rateLimit(` in the function; 496-511: `if (post && post.authorId !== session.user.id) { await prisma.notification.create({ data: { userId: post.authorId, type: "like", message: \`${session.user.name} liked your post\`, ... } }); }` runs on every create, unconditionally.
findings.fixDirection: Add a generous rateLimit bucket for engagement toggles (e.g. 60/10m per user) to toggleLike/toggleCommentLike/votePoll/toggleBookmark; dedupe the notification (skip create if an unread 'like' notification from this actor for this post already exists, or delete the notification on unlike).
findings.gateOrTest: Integration test: like-unlike-like the same post; assert the author holds exactly one like notification.
findings.reproPlan: Live with two test accounts: toggle a heart 5 times on the second account's post, open its bell — five identical rows.

findings.title: Account purge hard-deletes a member's comments, silently promoting other members' replies to top-level — the exact corruption the soft-delete design exists to prevent
findings.expected: Deleting an account removes the member's words the way deleteComment does: content blanked, row kept as structure, so surviving replies keep their "[deleted]" anchor and threads keep their shape.
findings.actual: purgeUserAccount runs `prisma.user.delete`, which cascades Comment rows via `author User @relation(..., onDelete: Cascade)`. The self-referencing parent relation has no onDelete, so it defaults to SetNull — and the schema's own comment on deletedAt states the consequence verbatim: "a hard delete would orphan them (the FK is SetNull, which silently promotes replies to top level) and the thread would lie about its shape." The owner hit this live on 2026-08-13 for single-comment deletes and the fix was the soft delete; the purge path (admin delete + 60-day retention sweep, both calling purgeUserAccount) re-introduces it wholesale: every reply anyone ever wrote under the purged member's comments becomes a context-free top-level comment.
findings.evidence: account-purge.ts 99-102: `await prisma.$transaction([ prisma.report.deleteMany({ where: { reporterId: userId } }), prisma.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } }) ]);` — no comment tombstoning. schema.prisma 447-450: `author User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)` and `parent Comment? @relation("CommentReplies", fields: [parentId], references: [id])` (no onDelete → SetNull), plus the 438-443 design comment quoted above.
findings.fixDirection: Before the user.delete in purgeUserAccount's transaction, soft-tombstone their comments instead of letting the cascade take them: `updateMany({ where: { authorId: userId }, data: { deletedAt: now, content: "" } })` will not survive the cascade, so either detach authorship (make Comment.authorId nullable with SetNull, matching AdminMessage's pattern) or excise the rows properly (delete their childless comments, tombstone the ones with replies by reassigning to a system user). The AdminMessage model (authorId String? with SetNull, comment: "Null ... for anyone whose account is later deleted") is the in-repo precedent.
findings.gateOrTest: Integration test: A comments, B replies, purge A → B's reply must still render under a [deleted] stub, not as a top-level comment.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (proving it live means purging an account against the shared production database).

findings.title: createPost and createComment double-submit windows: no unique guard exists for either, and the comment form lacks even the in-flight check
findings.expected: 6c: double-invocation before pending state disables the control must not create duplicate rows; the DB unique constraint is the only real guard.
findings.actual: Post and Comment have no unique constraint that could dedupe (nor could they, being free text), so the only guard is client pending state — and it is incomplete. CommentsSection.handleSubmit checks `if (!newComment.trim()) return;` but never `if (submitting) return` (contrast PollDisplay.handleVote, which has the guard); the submit control's `disabled` only takes effect after React re-renders, so two submissions in the same frame (Enter keydown + click, or key repeat racing the render) both reach createComment and write two identical comments plus two notifications. CreatePostForm.handleSubmit has the same missing guard (`if (!content.trim()) return;` then straight to work) with the same disabled-after-render window on the Post button — duplicates here are whole duplicate posts. Server-side nothing dedupes: rateLimit(10/10m posts, 30/10m comments) admits both.
findings.evidence: comments-section.tsx 181-184: `async function handleSubmit(e){ e.preventDefault(); if (!newComment.trim()) return; setSubmitting(true); ...` — no submitting check. create-post-form.tsx 497-500: `async function handleSubmit(saveAsDraft = false) { if (!content.trim()) return; if (saveAsDraft) setSavingDraft(true); else setSubmitting(true);` — same. poll-display.tsx:81 `if (submitting) return;` shows the intended pattern.
findings.fixDirection: Add `if (submitting || savingDraft) return;` as the first line of both handleSubmit functions (state read is the render-scope value, so also guard with a ref for same-frame safety: an inFlightRef.current check set synchronously). Optionally, server-side, a cheap recency dedupe (identical content by same author on same post within a few seconds → return the existing row) as backstop.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: dispatch two submit events in one tick on the comment form; assert one comment row appears.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account: hold Enter in the comment box on a slow connection (or dispatch form.requestSubmit() twice from the console) and observe duplicate comments.

findings.title: PollDisplay: tapping your already-chosen option optimistically inflates its count without adjusting the total (percentages exceed 100%)
findings.expected: Re-selecting the option you already voted for is a no-op visually.
findings.actual: handleVote's optimistic map gives the tapped option +1 in its first branch and only decrements prevVoted in the second — when they are the SAME option the +1 wins and no -1 happens, while localTotal is unchanged (`prevVoted ? t : t + 1`). One voter tapping their own choice renders 2 votes on the option over a total of 1 → the bar and CountUp show 200%. The server call succeeds (vote-switch to the same option), so the revert never runs and the lie persists until reload.
findings.evidence: poll-display.tsx 90-101: `voteCount: o.id === optionId ? o.voteCount + 1 : o.id === prevVoted ? o.voteCount - 1 : o.voteCount` — with optionId === prevVoted the first arm shadows the second; `setLocalTotal((t) => (prevVoted ? t : t + 1));` leaves the denominator alone.
findings.fixDirection: Early-return when `optionId === voted` (nothing to do), or make the map handle the equal case (net zero).
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: vote option A, tap A again, assert A's displayed count unchanged.
findings.reproPlan: Live, test account on a test poll: vote, then tap the same option — watch its percentage jump.

findings.title: PostFeed 'Load more' has no cancellation: a stale page from the previous filter/sort is appended after the filters change; offset sorts also duplicate rows across pages
findings.expected: Out-of-order completion never clobbers newer state (6b class 3), and a paginated list never renders one post twice.
findings.actual: handleLoadMore captures nothing to cancel: click Load more, then switch sort/search — the first-page effect (which DOES have a `cancelled` guard) replaces posts for the new filter, then the in-flight loadMore resolves and blindly runs `setPosts((prev) => [...prev, ...data.posts])`, appending old-filter posts under the new list, with cursor/hasMore overwritten by the stale response. Separately, the count-based sorts fall back to OFFSET paging (`skip: offset` while like/comment counts shift between requests), so a post can straddle a page boundary and appear twice; keys are `key={post.id}` with no dedupe in PostFeed (CommentsSection's mergeComments dedupes; PostFeed does not), producing React duplicate-key warnings and visibly duplicated cards.
findings.evidence: post-feed.tsx 152-159: `async function handleLoadMore() { setLoadingMore(true); const data = await fetchPosts(cursor); setPosts((prev) => [...prev, ...data.posts]); ... }` — no generation counter or cancelled flag; actions.ts 887-905 is the offset branch (`skip: offset` on a live-reordering orderBy).
findings.fixDirection: Keep a request-generation ref (incremented whenever filters change or a new fetch starts); handleLoadMore discards its response if the generation moved. Dedupe on append the way mergeComments does (filter incoming ids already present).
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: resolve a delayed loadMore after a filter change; assert posts contains only the new filter's page.
findings.reproPlan: Live: throttle network in devtools, click Load more, immediately switch to Most liked — old-sort posts append below the new list.

findings.title: Silent hard caps with no pagination: saved posts stop at 120, the letters index at 40 — older items become unreachable with no indication
findings.expected: Either pagination or an honest "showing the latest N" line on every capped list.
findings.actual: loadSavedPosts is `take: 120` with no cursor support and SavedPostsFeed fetches once with no load-more — a member's 121st-oldest bookmark silently ceases to exist anywhere in the UI (the header even asserts the visible count as the total: "{visibleCount} saved posts"). The letters index is `take: 40` with no load-more either; once the community passes 40 published letters, older ones are reachable only through feed search or a profile page. At 2,000 users over a few years both caps will be hit in normal use.
findings.evidence: actions.ts 963-980: `const rows = await prisma.bookmark.findMany({ ... orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 120, ...})` and no cursor parameter in the function signature; letters/page.tsx 60-62: `orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 40,` with no pagination UI in the render.
findings.fixDirection: Add keyset pagination to loadSavedPosts (cursor on bookmark createdAt/id) with a Load more in SavedPostsFeed; give the letters index either a Load more (same keyset shape loadPosts already implements) or reuse PostFeed with scope 'letters'.
findings.gateOrTest: Integration: seed 41 letters / 121 bookmarks for a test account and assert the UI can reach the oldest one.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only at current data volumes.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget DB writes in server components (feed search log, letter view counter) can die on serverless before committing; recordView also fires before the visibility checks
findings.expected: 6f: nothing runs after the response without after()/waitUntil — the codebase already knows this (createPost wraps its Collection copy in `after()`). Analytics writes should either use after() or accept documented loss; a view should only be recorded for content the viewer was actually allowed to see.
findings.actual: FeedPage runs `void logSearch({...})` and LetterPage runs `void recordView(session.user.id, "letter", letter.id)` as bare unawaited promises inside RSC render — on Vercel the function can freeze after the stream ends with the prisma write un-flushed, so both metrics undercount unpredictably (both helpers swallow their own errors, so nothing crashes — this is a loss, not a 500). Additionally recordView is called at line 85 BEFORE the draft/group/city notFound() checks at 91-106, so a member probing a private group letter's id records a "view" of content they were then refused; and unlike profiles (`if (kind === "profile" && viewerId === targetId) return`), letter self-views are counted, so an author polishing their own letter inflates its open count.
findings.evidence: feed/page.tsx 29-32: `if (q) { const s = await auth(); void logSearch({ scope: "feed", query: q, userId: s?.user?.id }); }`; letters/[id]/page.tsx 85 sits above `if (isDraft && !isAuthor) notFound();` at 93. content-view.ts 26: only the profile kind drops self-views.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap both calls in `after(() => ...)` (already imported and used in feed/actions.ts); move recordView below the last notFound() and add `viewerId === letter.authorId` to the self-view drop (or extend the kind check in recordView).
findings.gateOrTest: Code-review gate: grep for `void logSearch|void recordView` outside after() in server components.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (loss is probabilistic on serverless freeze).

findings.title: Blocked members' posts and comments remain in every feed under their linked name while the directory excludes them
findings.expected: A consistent policy for a blocked account's existing content: either it stays visible by explicit decision, or feeds filter it the way the directory does (schema comment on line 67: a deletion-requested account is "held out of the directory and search the same way a blocked one is").
findings.actual: `isBlocked` ends sessions (credentialVersion revocation) and hides the person from directory/search, but loadPosts/loadComments/letters queries have no `author: { isBlocked: false }` condition — a member blocked for abusive content keeps every post, comment and letter live in the feed with a working link to their profile until an admin soft-hides each item one by one. Suspected rather than confirmed as a defect because keep-content-visible is a defensible moderation policy; flagged because the directory and feed currently disagree and no comment records the choice.
findings.evidence: actions.ts baseWhere (822-832) filters `isHidden`, PUBLISHED_ONLY, batch, city — nothing about the author's standing; grep of the feed/letters queries finds no isBlocked reference anywhere in the territory.
findings.fixDirection: Owner decision first: if blocked content should vanish, add `author: { isBlocked: false }` to loadPosts/loadSavedPosts/loadComments/letters queries (indexed via the User pk join, cheap); if it should stay, record the decision in the schema comment so the asymmetry is deliberate.
findings.gateOrTest: Once decided: integration test blocking a fixture author and asserting feed behavior matches the decision.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (blocking a real account is an admin write).

6c votePoll cross-post option forgery: option-belongs-to-post is checked (`option.postId !== postId` refusal) — CLEAN
6c reportUser duplicate race: findFirst fast path + P2002 fallback returning alreadyFlagged is the exemplary pattern — CLEAN

6c server-action auth/ownership: every action in feed/actions.ts and report-action.ts re-checks session, and every interaction path (comment/like/bookmark/vote/loadComments) runs canViewPost/canViewPostOfComment — CLEAN

6d no interactive $transactions anywhere in the territory (the one $transaction, in account-purge, is array-form and pooler-safe); poll options created atomically via nested create (audit M32) — CLEAN

6h JSON-in-string parse sites: parseImageUrls, parseJsonArray, pollOptions parse, collectImageUrls, socialx parseUserLinks — every parse is try/caught with a safe empty fallback, including non-string array members — CLEAN
6h feed search: escapeLike applied to opts.search (LIKE wildcards), OR fragments composed into AND to avoid the bare-OR clobber, case-insensitivity gated on provider — CLEAN

6h keyset pagination correctness on the recent sort: stable (createdAt,id) ordering, concurrent-insert-above does not shift the cursor, page-beyond-end returns empty+hasMore:false correctly (the deleted-cursor row is the one failure, reported) — CLEAN

6h batch-key substring collisions in targetBatches contains-matching: ICSE/ISC year keys cannot be substrings of each other; checked against the only batchType values the codebase produces (batchTypeFromLeaving: 'ISC' | 'ICSE' | null) — CLEAN

6h comment thread pagination: replies always travel with their page's parents, deleted/hidden roots stubbed so replies keep anchors, mergeComments dedupes a fresh own comment against later pages, take clamped 1..50 — CLEAN

6h draft leakage: PUBLISHED_ONLY spread across loadPosts/loadSavedPosts/letters index; letters/[id] denies drafts to non-authors with the same 404; /letters/[id]/edit is author+draft only; drafts excluded from Collection copy — CLEAN

6h comment counts vs soft delete: _count.comments filters {isHidden:false, deletedAt:null} in loadPosts, loadSavedPosts and the letter page, and the client removeLocally mirrors the server stub/count rules exactly (checked all four delete cases) — CLEAN
markFeedSeen monotonic conditional updateMany (two devices cannot rewind each other), NaN-date guarded, failure silent-in-prod/loud-in-dev — CLEAN
recordView upsert P2002 race is swallowed by its own try/catch (never throws) — CLEAN
loadComments visibility: requires session AND canViewPost, returns the indistinguishable empty page for missing vs forbidden post ids — CLEAN
loadSavedPosts privacy: session-scoped bookmarks only, group membership and cityScope re-checked on read-back — CLEAN

editPost image rewrite authorization: draft-only, letter-only, ownership-checked on newly added URLs with grandfathering for legacy keys, cap 3, malformed field ignored — CLEAN (the R2 orphan on replacement is reported separately)
renderRichText escape-then-transform ordering, strict mention-id charset, capped lazy emphasis quantifier (no catastrophic backtracking) — re-examined, CLEAN (and covered by the security audit)

Upload path in the composer: 20MB pre-check, sequential uploads with per-file error isolation, abort timeout on the proxied fallback, preview/url arrays kept aligned — CLEAN

Skimmed by grep: docs/spec/letters.md (cap/draft/targeting decisions), docs/planning/bugs.md (full read, to exclude tracked items — notably the letters-index toLocaleDateString display shift, which is item 6's own note and was therefore NOT re-reported; only the deeper query-window IST instance was), prisma/migrations-manual/ (index census), src/app/api tree (confirming no orphan-sweep cron exists). Consciously skipped as other investigators' territory: /api/upload presign/finalize internals, groups/catchups surfaces (only their intersection with loadPosts/votePoll checked), auth.ts/rate-limit.ts uncommitted deltas beyond what the feed calls, letter-desk.tsx and letters/new client shell (thin wrappers over CreatePostForm, which was read fully), LetterImages/ImageViewer/ShareButton/BookmarkButton internals (BookmarkButton's guard-absence was grepped), and admin-content queries.
